prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values and approach
- Freedom, Justice, Honesty: expand opportunity, ensure fairness, and be upfront about costs.
- Invest in core public services and the environment; empower professionals; devolve power; cut needless central interference.

Health and care
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied professionals; add 10,000 beds; raise pay for the lowest-paid NHS staff.
- Shift to prevention: more scanners; restore free NHS dental and eye checks; expand tests in primary care; support complementary medicine.
- Free personal care for the elderly/long-term needs; end the “postcode lottery” via a new Pharmaceutical Agency; expand mental health and social care; no-fault compensation; more local accountability.

Education, skills and jobs
- Primary classes averaging 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (25,000 in KS1); paid preparation time; scrap PRP; reduce bureaucracy; reform inspections and testing (end SATs at 7).
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for the poorest; raise loan repayment threshold; improve access and staff pay.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 2 for adults; to Level 3 for 16–24s); training incentives for SMEs; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace New Deal with a flexible, universal job-matching service.

Law, policing and justice
- 6,000 more police; 2,000 part-time community officers; a Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints system.
- Focus on prevention and rehabilitation; more community sentences; work, skills and literacy in prisons; stronger victims’ rights; retain jury trials; end most mandatory sentences; tackle hate crime.

Transport and environment
- Free off-peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; aim for half-price fares for under-19s in education.
- Abolish car tax for the cleanest vehicles; no real-terms fuel duty rise; empower councils on congestion charging and bonds.
- Stronger public control of rail: restructure Railtrack to a not-for-profit model; create a Sustainable Transport Authority; modernise London Underground via a not-for-profit bond model.
- Green thread: carbon tax to replace the Climate Change Levy; at least 10% renewable electricity by 2010, rising annually; phase out nuclear as stations retire; major recycling push and brownfield-first development.

Pensions, wages and benefits
- Immediate pension rise: +£5/week (single), with larger boosts for over-75s/80s; funded by a 50% tax rate on income over £100k; create an Independent Pensions Authority.
- Equal minimum wage for 16+ with annual review; targeted child poverty payments; fairer housing benefit and utility tariffs; plan to lift lowest earners out of tax over time.

Democracy, rights and communities
- Fair votes: AV+ referendum for Westminster; STV for local/European; elected Senate to replace Lords; stronger Parliament and FOI; votes at 16; civil service protections.
- Equality Act banning all discrimination; repeal Section 28; humane, faster asylum with fair cash benefits; no ID cards; civil partnership registration; animal welfare reforms.
- Deeper devolution (nations/regions); replace Council Tax with local income tax; empower local regeneration; support farming (CAP reform, organic shift) and fisheries (local management).

Europe, economy and defence
- Pro-EU reform and enlargement; euro entry via referendum at a sustainable rate; more democratic EU institutions.
- One penny on income tax for education; 50% top rate for pensions/NHS; CGT reforms; household “Citizen’s Tax Contract”; stronger, more independent Bank of England.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing global disarmament; oppose US NMD; ethical foreign policy, end subsidies for arms exports; meet 0.7% aid target, fairer trade, debt relief, and major action on HIV/AIDS.
